Estimate conditional treatment effect scores

Source: R/CATE.R
catefit.Rd

Estimate CATE scores for binary, count and survival outcomes. Binary scores include arm-specific logistic regression, doubly robust two-regression estimation and boosting. Count and survival methods include both outcome-regression and doubly robust scores. Continuous outcomes are not yet implemented.

Usage

catefit(
  response,
  data,
  outcome_model,
  outcome_method = NULL,
  benefit_model = NULL,
  benefit_method = NULL,
  ps_model,
  ps_method = "glm",
  ipcw.model = NULL,
  ipcw.method = "breslow",
  minPS = 0.01,
  maxPS = 0.99,
  followup.time = NULL,
  tau0 = NULL,
  higher.y = TRUE,
  prop.cutoff = seq(0.5, 1, length = 6),
  surv.min = 0.025,
  xvar.smooth.score = NULL,
  xvar.smooth.init = NULL,
  tree.depth = 2,
  n.trees.rf = 1000,
  n.trees.boosting = 200,
  B = 3,
  Kfold = 5,
  error.maxNR = 0.001,
  max.iterNR = 150,
  tune = c(0.5, 2),
  seed = NULL,
  plot.gbmperf = FALSE,
  verbose = 0,
  contrast.control = list(),
  rmst.control = list(),
  ps.control = list(),
  rf.control = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

response

A string describing the type of outcome in the data. Allowed values include "binary" (see catefitbinary), "count" (see catefitcount), "survival" (see catefitsurv), and "continuous" (not implemented).

data

A data frame containing the variables in the outcome, treatment, and censoring models (if specified); a data frame with n rows (1 row per observation).

outcome_model

A formula describing the outcome and covariates for outcome models. The outcome must appear on the left-hand side. For survival outcomes, a Surv object must be used to describe the outcome.

outcome_method

Outcome-model method, with one entry per benefit_method. For a T-learner, NULL selects "logistic" for binary, "poisson" for count, and "coxph" for survival outcomes. Specify a method for two-regression or contrast regression. When both are fitted together, they may use different outcome methods. See catefitbinary, catefitcount, or catefitsurv for the available methods and their assumptions.

benefit_model

Optional one-sided formula specifying the covariates and terms for the two-regression or contrast-regression score. The default NULL uses the covariates and terms of outcome_model. An intercept is required and offsets are not supported. T-learner scores use the outcome model directly and do not use this formula. In a mixed fit it applies only to two-regression and contrast regression. Continuous-outcome fitting is not implemented.

benefit_method

A vector of score-construction methods (default "t_learner"): "t_learner", "two_regression", or "contrast_regression". Each is paired with the corresponding entry in outcome_method. Contrast regression is not available for binary outcomes. Continuous outcomes are not implemented. The previous method names "twoReg" and "contrastReg" are accepted as aliases for "two_regression" and "contrast_regression", respectively.

ps_model

A formula describing the treatment model (propensity-score model) to be fitted. The treatment must appear on the left-hand side. For binary outcomes, logical treatment values FALSE and TRUE are mapped to 0 and 1, respectively. Numeric 0/1 values or two distinct treatment labels are also accepted. If data are from a randomized controlled trial, specify ps_model = trt ~ 1 as an intercept-only model.

ps_method

A character value for the method to estimate the propensity score. Allowed values include one of: 'glm' for logistic regression with main effects only (default), or 'lasso' for a logistic regression with main effects and LASSO penalization on two-way interactions (added to the model if interactions are not specified in ps_model). Relevant only when ps_model has more than one variable.

ipcw.model

A formula describing the censoring model used for inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW). The left-hand side must be empty. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is NULL, which uses a censoring model with the same covariates as the outcome model outcome_model, plus the treatment.

ipcw.method

A character value for the censoring model. Only applies for survival outcomes. Allowed values are: 'breslow' (Cox regression with Breslow estimator of t he baseline survivor function), 'aft (exponential)', 'aft (weibull)', 'aft (lognormal)' or 'aft (loglogistic)' (accelerated failure time model with different distributions for y variable). Default is 'breslow'.

minPS

A numerical value (in `[0, 1]`) below which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Default is 0.01.

maxPS

A numerical value (in `(0, 1]`) above which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Must be strictly greater than minPS. Default is 0.99.

followup.time

A column name in data specifying the maximum follow-up time, interpreted as the potential censoring time. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is NULL, which corresponds to unknown potential censoring time.

tau0

The truncation time for defining restricted mean time lost. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is NULL, which corresponds to setting the truncation time as the maximum survival time in the data.

higher.y

A logical value indicating whether higher (TRUE) or lower (FALSE) values of the outcome are more desirable. Default is TRUE.

prop.cutoff

A vector of numerical values (in `(0, 1]`) specifying percentiles of the estimated CATE scores to define nested subgroups. Each element represents the cutoff to separate observations in nested subgroups (below vs above cutoff). The length of prop.cutoff is the number of nested subgroups. An equally-spaced sequence of proportions ending with 1 is recommended. Default is seq(0.5, 1, length = 6).

surv.min

Lower truncation limit for the probability of remaining uncensored, used in IPCW. It must be a positive value and should be chosen close to 0. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is 0.025.

xvar.smooth.score

A vector of characters indicating the name of the variables used as the smooth terms if score.method = 'gam'. The variables must be selected from the variables listed in outcome_model.

xvar.smooth.init

A vector of characters indicating the name of the variables used as the smooth terms if outcome_method = 'gam'. The variables must be selected from the variables listed in outcome_model. Default is NULL, which uses all variables in outcome_model.

tree.depth

A positive integer specifying the maximum depth of boosting trees. Used when outcome_method = 'boosting'. Default is 2.

n.trees.rf

A positive integer specifying the number of trees in random forest. Used if score.method = 'randomForest' or if outcome_method = 'random_forest' with score.method = 'twoReg' or 'contrastReg'. Only applies for survival outcomes. Default is 1000.

n.trees.boosting

The maximum number of boosting trees, used when outcome_method = 'boosting'. Default is 200.

B

Number of repetitions of cross-fitting for benefit_method = 'two_regression' or 'contrast_regression'. Default is 3.

Kfold

A positive integer specifying the number of folds used in cross-fitting to partition the data in benefit_method = 'two_regression' and 'contrast_regression'. Default is 5.

error.maxNR

Convergence tolerance for the Newton-Raphson algorithm used by benefit_method = 'contrast_regression'. Default is 0.001.

max.iterNR

A positive integer indicating the maximum number of iterations in the Newton Raphson algorithm. Used only if benefit_method = 'contrast_regression'. Default is 150.

tune

A vector of 2 numerical values > 0 specifying tuning parameters for the Newton Raphson algorithm. tune[1] is the step size, tune[2] specifies a quantity to be added to diagonal of the slope matrix to prevent singularity. Used only if benefit_method = 'contrast_regression'. Default is c(0.5, 2).

seed

An optional integer specifying an initial randomization seed for reproducibility. Default is NULL, corresponding to no seed.

plot.gbmperf

Whether to plot boosting performance measures when outcome_method = 'boosting'. Default is FALSE.

verbose

An integer value indicating whether intermediate progress messages and histograms should be printed. 1 indicates messages are printed and 0 otherwise. Default is 0.

contrast.control

A named list of options for count or survival contrast regression. Supported names are solver ("C", the default, or "R"), error.maxNR, max.iterNR, tune, and optim.control (a named list passed to stats::optim on fallback). List entries override the corresponding top-level NR arguments. Options are kept separate from ..., which is forwarded to boosting. Count and survival outcomes support this list; continuous outcomes retain their existing solver.

rmst.control

Named options for Cox restricted mean survival integration. Supported entry: solver = "C" (default) or solver = "R". The C backend accumulates each patient's integral without allocating a patient-by-event-time matrix. Cox model fitting is unchanged. Available only for survival outcomes; independent of contrast.control.

ps.control

Named options for LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Supported entry: solver = "C" (default) or solver = "R". Only affects screening when ps_method = "lasso"; the LASSO fit and interaction selection rule are unchanged. Kept separate from boosting's ... and other numerical controls.

rf.control

Named list of randomForestSRC options: mtry, nodesize, nsplit, nodedepth, and splitrule. Applies to both treatment arms and survival initial-predictor forests. Use n.trees.rf for the number of trees.

...

The legacy init.model argument supplies a separate initial outcome formula using the previous interface, where outcome_model defines the score. It cannot be combined with benefit_model. The legacy initial.predictor.method is accepted with a deprecation warning and cannot be supplied together with outcome_method. Legacy arguments ps.model and ps.method are accepted with warnings. Additional boosting arguments; see boosting-control. The old named arguments score.method and cate.model are accepted with deprecation warnings. Legacy score names and positional calls remain supported when outcome_method is omitted.

Value

Fitted objects retain treatment.labels in treatment 0/1 order for score plot labels. For binary response, see catefitbinary(). For count response, see description of other outputs in catefitcount(). For survival response, see description of outputs in catefitsurv().

Details

The table summarizes the available score-fitting methods. "Yes" in the final column indicates a doubly robust score estimator, subject to the assumptions described below; "–" means that the method is not available for that outcome.

Score methodBinaryCountSurvivalDoubly robust
twoRegYesYesYesYes
contrastReg–YesYesYes
logisticYes––No
poisson–YesYesNo
negBin–Yes–No
boostingYesYesYesNo
randomForest––YesNo
coxph, weibull, log_normal––YesNo

Two-regression and contrast regression share cross-fitted treatment-model predictions. When their outcome methods match, they also share the cross-fitted outcome predictions; otherwise, each outcome method is fitted separately on the same folds. A T-learner uses outcome models fitted on the full fitting sample, so it does not reuse the cross-fitted models. When two distinct initial outcome methods are used, outcome_methods records the method for each score. For stochastic outcome methods, random-number consumption can differ from fitting each score in a separate call.

The doubly robust methods combine outcome and treatment models. Their robustness to misspecification of one of these models is conditional on identification, positivity, and method-specific model and regularity assumptions. For example, binary twoReg estimates a linear projection of the conditional risk difference; this projection equals the conditional risk difference only if the latter is linear in the specified design. Truncating propensity scores can affect the robustness property. Survival methods also require appropriate censoring assumptions and a correctly specified censoring model.

This table describes score fitting. Subgroup effects can be estimated using doubly robust methods even when the score used to define the subgroups is not doubly robust. Neither score fitting nor subgroup estimates calculated on the fitting data constitute independent validation; see catecv.

For binary response, see the Binary outcomes section below and catefitbinary(). For count response, see details in catefitcount(). For survival response, see details in catefitsurv().

Binary outcomes

For response = "binary", score.method = "logistic" fits a separate logistic outcome model in each treatment arm and subtracts their predicted risks. "twoReg" cross-fits separate logistic outcome models and a treatment model, then projects the augmented inverse-propensity outcomes for each arm onto the covariates in benefit_model (or outcome_model by default) using linear regression. The score is the difference of these projections, averaged over B repetitions of Kfold folds. It estimates the linear projection of the conditional risk difference if either the treatment model or both outcome models are correct, under identification and positivity assumptions. Propensity score truncation can affect this property. The projection need not lie between -1 and 1 and equals the conditional risk difference only if that difference is linear in the specified design. The difference between arm coefficients is returned in coefficients$twoReg and by coef(); the separate arm coefficients are stored in fit$twoReg$coefficients. Logistic model coefficients for each arm are on the log-odds scale and stored in fit$logistic; they are not linear risk-difference score coefficients. Boosting does not have a linear score coefficient vector. With neither twoReg nor another linear binary score, coef() returns NULL. "boosting" fits separate Bernoulli gradient-boosting models in each treatment arm, with the number of trees selected by five-fold cross-validation. All three scores are predicted risk differences; subgroup effects are doubly robust risk differences. Binary boosting requires at least one outcome-model covariate and both outcome values in each arm. Its fitted models and selected tree counts are stored in fit$boosting. Scores and subgroup effects are estimated on the same data; they are not independent validation. For extra boosting controls, see boosting-control. Subgroup fits without both arms or with rank-deficient models return NA.

Examples

# Count outcome
fit_1 <- catefit(response = "count",
                 data = countExample,
                 outcome_model = y ~ age + female + previous_treatment +
                                  previous_cost + previous_number_relapses +
                                  offset(log(years)),
                 outcome_method = "poisson",
                 benefit_method = "t_learner",
                 ps_model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,
                 higher.y = TRUE,
                 seed = 999)
#> Variable trt was recoded to 0/1 with drug0->0 and drug1->1.

coef(fit_1)
#>                              poisson
#> (Intercept)              -0.58185218
#> age                      -0.01117701
#> female                    0.58829733
#> previous_treatmentdrugB   0.73724361
#> previous_treatmentdrugC   0.15545985
#> previous_cost            -0.13035642
#> previous_number_relapses -0.05339112

# \donttest{
# Survival outcome
library(survival)
tau0 <- with(survivalExample,
                 min(quantile(y[trt == "drug1"], 0.95), quantile(y[trt == "drug0"], 0.95)))

fit_2 <- catefit(response = "survival",
                 data = survivalExample,
                 outcome_model = Surv(y, d) ~ age + female + previous_cost +
                                           previous_number_relapses,
                 outcome_method = c("poisson", "boosting", "random_forest"),
                 benefit_method = rep("t_learner", 3),
                 ps_model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,
                 #'                  ipcw.model = ~ age + previous_cost + previous_treatment,
                 tau0 = tau0, higher.y = TRUE, seed = 999, n.cores = 1)
#> Variable trt was recoded to 0/1 with drug0->0 and drug1->1.
#>     Warning: Warning(s) occurred when estimating the ATEs in the nested subgroup using "poisson", "boosting" 
#> Warning: Warning: Warning(s) occurred when estimating the ATEs in the nested subgroup using "poisson", "boosting"; see 'errors/warnings'.

coef(fit_2)
#>                              poisson
#> (Intercept)               0.45047296
#> age                      -0.24616564
#> female                    0.11776100
#> previous_cost             0.87728869
#> previous_number_relapses -0.03975634

# }
